title: BP 220 Parks, Playgrounds, and Road Pavement
subject: Planning / Housing / Building Laws

questions.stem: In the cited BP 220 IRR hierarchy of basic needs, which item comes first?

rationale.correct: The extracted list places water first among the basic needs of human settlements.

distractors.A: Park/playground appears later in the list.
distractors.C: Power appears after park/playground in the extracted sequence.
distractors.D: Solid/liquid waste disposal is listed, but not first.

rationale.takeaway: For hierarchy stems, answer from the sequence, not from what sounds most visible on a site plan.

questions.stem: For 150 lots/dwelling units per hectare and below, what parks/playgrounds allocation is shown in Table 1?

rationale.correct: Table 1 shows 3.5% of gross area for parks/playgrounds at 150 and below.

distractors.A: 1.0% belongs to a different facility allocation context, not this parks/playgrounds row.
distractors.B: 2.0% is not the cited parks/playgrounds value for 150 and below.
distractors.D: 7.0% appears at a higher density band.

rationale.takeaway: Use the density row before selecting the percentage.

questions.source_locator: BP 220 Revised IRR 2008, Table 1, PDF p.12.

questions.stem: Under the cited BP 220 road-pavement excerpt, what minimum asphalt thickness is stated for major/minor roads and motor courts?

rationale.correct: The excerpt states asphalt with minimum thickness of 50 mm; concrete is the 150 mm value.

distractors.A: 25 mm is not the cited value.
distractors.C: 100 mm is not stated in the excerpt.
distractors.D: 150 mm is the concrete thickness, not asphalt.

rationale.takeaway: Pair the material with the correct thickness: asphalt 50 mm, concrete 150 mm.

questions.source_locator: BP 220 Revised IRR 2008, Section 5.b.3.4, PDF p.17.
